headline: Middle East Tensions Set the Tone as Geopolitical Risk Creeps Back Into Pre-Market Trading
body_html:
Futures are trading cautiously ahead of Thursday's open as investors digest a fresh round of geopolitical headlines centered on the Middle East. Oil climbed to a three-week high overnight after shipping data suggested Hormuz corridor flows remain fragile, and Washington's warnings of economic consequences for nations that back Iran are keeping risk appetite measured. The energy complex will be closely watched at the bell, with any escalation language likely to amplify crude's move.

Wednesday's completed session offered an encouraging underlying picture: 327 names in the universe advanced against 218 decliners, and seven of eight tracked sectors finished in positive territory. Homebuilders led the way with a 3.24% gain, followed by Healthcare at 2.49%. The lone drag was Semiconductors, which shed 2.75% — a pocket of weakness that could set the tone for chip-adjacent names early Thursday given persistent macro uncertainty.

On the catalyst front, traders will be watching for any fresh diplomatic signals from Washington regarding Iran, as well as follow-through from Wednesday's standout movers in pharma and telehealth. Pre-market positioning looks tentative; headline risk from the Middle East remains the dominant variable at the open.

briefs.headline: Oil Reaches Three-Week Peak on Supply-Route Anxiety
briefs.body: Crude prices hit their highest level in three weeks overnight as traders priced in heightened risk around Middle Eastern supply corridors. Shipping data through the Strait of Hormuz shows no immediate disruption, but the standoff between Washington and Tehran is keeping a risk premium embedded in energy markets. Energy stocks closed up 0.63% on Wednesday and may extend gains at Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Washington Issues Stark Warning Over Iran Alliances
briefs.body: The White House signaled it is prepared to impose economic consequences on any country that provides support to Iran, a statement that landed overnight and is reverberating across emerging-market currencies and commodity desks. The warning adds another layer of uncertainty for multinationals with exposure to the region and could weigh on sentiment in early Thursday trading.

briefs.headline: Chip Sector Drags as Broad Market Otherwise Holds Firm
briefs.body: Semiconductors were the clear outlier in Wednesday's session, falling 2.75% while every other tracked sector posted gains. Several storage and power-module names fell sharply, with Seagate Technology dropping 7.87% and Vicor Corporation sliding 10.34%. Traders will be watching whether any pre-market stabilization emerges in the complex before Thursday's open.

briefs.headline: Merck Surges to Record, Booking Outsized Gains for Holders
briefs.body: Merck shares surged 12.60% on Wednesday, reaching record highs and allowing investors to lock in multifold profits on what has been one of the year's strongest pharma runs. The move lifted the broader Healthcare sector by 2.49% and added momentum to the telehealth space, where Hims & Hers Health rose 13.51% on the same session.

briefs.headline: Estee Lauder Leads Consumer Gainers With Double-Digit Advance
briefs.body: The beauty and personal-care segment got a jolt on Wednesday as Estee Lauder surged 16.30%, easily topping the day's leaderboard across the universe. The move helped lift the broader Consumer sector to a 1.47% gain. Whether the rally reflects a fundamental re-rating or short-covering will be a key question heading into Thursday.

briefs.headline: La-Z-Boy Tumbles, Leading a Cluster of Consumer and Industrial Declines
briefs.body: La-Z-Boy fell 16.95% on Wednesday, the steepest single-session decline in the universe, as the furniture retailer appeared to disappoint the market. The drop came alongside weakness in Steel Dynamics, off 7.53%, underscoring that while breadth was positive overall, pockets of cyclical selling were pronounced. Both names will be monitored for stabilization signals at Thursday's open.
